1.
List has been revised.
2. Heard Sri Devaang Savla, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri R.P. Patel, learned State Law Officer and perused the record.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No. 724 of 2024, under Sections 376, 506 I.P.C., Police Station Majhola, District Moradabad, during the pendency of trial.

sentences.text: The applicant is stated to be the brother-in-law (devar) of the victim.
The husband of the victim had expired during COVID-19 pandemic.
The applicant is stated to have committed rape with the victim and subsequently promised her to marry but refused to comply with the said promise of marriage in the year 2022.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF APPLICANT :
5. The applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case and he has nothing to do with the said offence.
6. The FIR is delayed by about two years and there is no explanation of the said delay caused.
7.

Initially, the said informant had filed a Complaint Case No.39266 of 2022 against the applicant and other family members under sections 498A, 323, 427, 406, 504, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 of the D.P. Act, Police Station-Katghar, before the court of A.C.J.M. Court No.4, Moradabad.
8. After having failed in the said complaint case, the victim has instituted the instant FIR.
9. The said complaint case which has been filed as Annexure-9 to the affidavit does not whisper a single word about any sexual assault being committed to her.

10. The instant FIR is hit by Section 337 of B.N.S.
11.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
12. There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 24.09.2024.
The applicant is ready to cooperate with trial.

In case, the applicant is released on bail,
he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF STATE :
13. The bail application has been opposed but the submissions raised by the learned counsel for the applicant could not be disputed.
CONCLUSION:

14. Learned counsel has placed much reliance upon the judgement of Supreme Court passed in Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam Vs. The State of Bihar, reported in 2022(6) SCC 599 and has categorically stated that the Courts should be careful in proceeding against the distant relatives in crimes pertaining to matrimonial disputes and dowry deaths.

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam Vs. The State of Bihar, reported in 2022(6) SCC 599
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The relatives of the husband should not be roped in on the basis of omnibus allegations unless specific instances of their involvement in the crime are made out.

sentences.text: In light of the judgement of the Supreme Court passed in Niranjan Singh and another vs Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and others AIR 1980 SC 785, this Court has avoided detailed examination of the evidence and elaborate documentation of the merits of the case as no party should have the impression that his case has been prejudiced.

entities.text: Niranjan Singh and another vs Prabhakar Rajaram Kharote and others AIR 1980 SC 785
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A prima facie satisfaction of case is needed but it is not the same as an exhaustive exploration of the merits in the order itself.
16. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

17. A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
18.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that "bail is a rule and jail is an exception".
19.
Learned State Law Officer could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
20. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned State Law Officer.

21. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

22. Let the applicant- Kuldeep Kashyap involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C./351 B.N.S.S.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Kuldeep Kashyap vs State Of U.P. on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76368914/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
23. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

24. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
